parsed_response.reasoning: The diff confirms the mechanism: CalendarManager's createEvent now takes externalId and calls calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id), while BaseCalendarService.createEvent still filters calendars by mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId (the FIRST destination calendar's externalId) and ignores the credentialId/externalId parameters. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents iterates all destinations and calls createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId) per host. For a CalDAV-type host after the first, the credential's calendars won't match the first host's externalId, so the filter drops them all and no event is created — a silent correctness gap in the very multi-host feature this PR adds. GoogleCalendarService was updated to find by credentialId; the base class was not.

judged_text: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the credential's calendars to those matching only the FIRST destination calendar's externalId, ignoring the credentialId parameter and the per-destination externalId the new flow passes (GoogleCalendarService got credentialId matching; this base class did not). For a collective booking with multiple CalDAV-type hosts (Apple/Nextcloud/Fastmail), the createEvent call made with a non-first host's credential filters out all of that host's calendars because they don't match the first host's externalId, so no event is created on their calendar at all — the multi-host feature silently produces nothing for every host after the first.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows BaseCalendarService.createEvent now derives `mainHostDestinationCalendar` via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and filters CalDAV calendars with `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts). Meanwhile, the new multi-destination flow builds `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array (often organizer first, then other hosts) and EventManager creates events per destination/credential (packages/core/EventManager.ts), but CalendarManager only passes `credential.id` into `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and does not pass the per-destination externalId to BaseCalendarService. Unlike GoogleCalendarService (which selects a destination calendar by matching `credentialId` in `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.find(...)`), BaseCalendarService always uses the FIRST destination calendar externalId, so for non-first host credentials its `.filter(...)` can eliminate all calendars, resulting in no event being created for those hosts.
